# moddotplot-rs v0.1.0

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

moddotplot-rs v0.1 is the first functional preview of the install-free genomic
dotplot. It accepts local FASTA input, computes containment-derived identity in a
browser worker, and supports responsive progressive exploration without uploading
sequence data.

The canonical software authorship statement is maintained in
[project provenance](../PROVENANCE.md).
Users are requested to cite the original ModDotPlot paper and the relevant scientific
methods listed in the [citation guide](../CITATIONS.md).

## Highlights

* Independent sequence selection on the X and Y axes, including self-comparisons
* ntHash2 and word-parallel OPH/b-bit sketches with HLL cardinality
* A 256-register default quick view followed by 2,048-register detailed refinement
* Bounded exact correction for sparse detailed windows based on a 99% match-detection
  target at the 80% ANI operating floor
* 256 by 256 on-demand tiles, adjacent prefetch, cancellation, immutable tile keys, and
  byte-budgeted caches
* Similarity and forward/reverse coloring from the same numeric tiles
* Exact canonical k-mer matching at terminal zoom
* BED3-12, GFF3, and GTF feature tracks with sequence-name and coordinate validation
* Entirely static deployment with no application backend or runtime JavaScript library

## Validation snapshot

The prepared working tree passes 57 Rust tests and 19 TypeScript tests, strict Clippy,
the Wasm target check, and the production Wasm and browser builds. The optimized Wasm
payload is 153.20 kB before transport compression and 65.55 kB gzip in the Vite report.
Validation used Rust/Cargo 1.98.0, Node.js 25.9.0, npm 11.12.1, and wasm-pack 0.15.0.
These commands must be rerun on the final reviewed release commit before tagging.

The Phase 0 harness includes synthetic fixtures and a CHM13 repeat sample. The exact
all-k-mer containment score is the primary oracle; MashMap bottom-s and minmer paths
serve as independent references.

## Preview limitations

This release is not yet described as research-validated. The following work remains:

* Sharded sequence/sketch storage and bounded disk spill before claiming robust 1 Gb
  record support
* A current CHM13 benchmark for the separated progressive pipeline
* Broader validation of the probability-based sparse correction policy
* Automated cross-browser visual, worker-failure, and WebGL recovery testing
* Numeric and high-resolution image export
* Session persistence

See the [implementation status](../STATUS.md) and
[release checklist](../RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md) for the complete evidence and gate list.

## Build from source

The release requires a current Rust toolchain, the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target,
`wasm-pack`, Node.js 22 or newer, and npm:

```sh
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build:wasm
npm --prefix web run build
```

Deploy `web/dist/` through an HTTP or HTTPS static host.
